notes_for_test_design_validator: The full resolvePersonalCodeIdentity rule table (docs/agents/design/REQ-040.md §2.2) is exercised case-by-case in the domain file's AC6/AC7 describe blocks: not-found, bulk/companion-not-applicable, target-already-linked-not-applicable, own-row-null-tgId link (the normal case), the idempotent-second-tap concurrency fallback, plain collision-relink, multi-event collision-relink, and the schema-conflict collision-relink (REQ-040-schema.md §4.2's two-statement conditional-repoint-then-delete sequence, traced against a constructed uniqueness conflict where B already holds an entry for one of A's events).

The opened_at/derived-status semantics are covered twice deliberately: domain-level (AC3/AC4, constructing each state directly and asserting listInviteListEntries's derivation) and end-to-end (handler file's AC6 describe block, which drives a real /start deep-link tap through markInviteListEntryOpened and confirms opened_at is non-null even though the entry's rendered status has since advanced to 'registered').

No test in either file asserts on literal English/Russian copy text (only on structural properties: which values are/aren't present, button-label sets, row counts, ids) except where the catalog constant itself is imported and compared (catalog.inviteList.*, catalog.inviteCodes.eventCancelled/eventFinished) -- a future copy change does not require touching these tests, matching REQ-039's own stated discipline.

AC9's 'no send action' is verified statically (no NotificationSender import, no sender. call site) rather than by asserting an empty captured-messages list at runtime, because the handler file's own happy-path/S2 cases already prove every reply lands on ctx (the organizer's own chat) as a side effect of asserting on lastSendMessage/answerCallbackQuery content -- the static check is the one that would actually fail if a future change added a stray send call, which a runtime assertion scoped to one test's own captured array would not reliably catch.
